bindings.note: Consumed in nz/regulations/acc/earners_levy.yaml by acc_standard_earners_levy_excluding_gst (source: Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations 2025 regs 4, 5 and 8): 'min(max(0, acc_earnings_for_earners_levy), acc_earners_levy_maximum_earnings) * acc_earners_levy_rate_excluding_gst', and by acc_standard_earners_levy_including_gst (IRD PAYE-facing rate, rounded to cents). The module's test standard_negative_earnings feeds -100 and expects a nil levy, so the input admits a net loss. Read here as annual gross employee wages plus net non-farm and farm self-employment profit. Differences: the input is 'earnings' in the Accident Compensation Act sense (the definition is not in this module), a legal quantity; the concept's gross wages (with tips, bonuses, commissions) may not match the Act's earnings items; shareholder-employee earnings are not separated in the concepts; and this sum nets a self-employment loss against wages before the rule clamps at zero, which the module does not say the Act does. Both annual.

Consumed in nz/regulations/acc/earners_levy.yaml by acc_low_self_employed_minimum_levy_excluding_gst (source: Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations 2025 reg 6): 'if acc_self_employed_more_than_30_hours_per_week and acc_self_employed_earnings_for_earners_levy < acc_low_self_employed_minimum_earnings: acc_earners_levy_rate_excluding_gst * max(0, acc_low_self_employed_minimum_earnings - acc_employee_earnings_for_low_self_employed_formula)'. Read as the person's annual gross wages and salaries. Differences: the input is employee earnings as the Accident Compensation Act defines them (not in this module); the concept is the survey's gross employee cash income. Both annual. The gating flag (self-employed more than 30 hours a week) stays uncovered, so this binding only matters once it is set.

Consumed in nz/regulations/acc/earners_levy.yaml by acc_low_self_employed_minimum_levy_excluding_gst (source: Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations 2025 reg 6), which applies the minimum-earnings formula when 'acc_self_employed_earnings_for_earners_levy < acc_low_self_employed_minimum_earnings' for a person self-employed more than 30 hours a week. Read as annual net non-farm plus farm self-employment profit. Differences: the input is self-employed earnings as the Accident Compensation Act defines them (not in this module), a legal quantity; shareholder-employee earnings are not identifiable in the concepts and are not included. Both annual; the concepts are signed and the rule compares the value as given.

Consumed in nz/regulations/health_entitlement_cards/community_services_card/core.yaml by community_services_card_family_group_for_dependent_child_threshold (source: Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 reg 8(7)): '... and community_services_card_dependent_children_count >= 1', and by community_services_card_no_dependent_children_income_route (reg 8(1)(d)): 'community_services_card_dependent_children_count == 0 and ...'. Read as the number of co-resident persons aged 17 or under who name this person as a parent (birth, adoptive or step). Differences: the regulations' dependent-child definition is not in this module and the 17 cut is this mapping's assumption; a partner's child not recorded as this person's stepchild, and a non-parent caregiver's child, are missed.

Consumed in nz/regulations/health_entitlement_cards/community_services_card/core.yaml by community_services_card_no_dependent_children_income_route (source: Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 reg 8(1)(d)): '... and community_services_card_person_age_years >= community_services_card_minimum_age_without_dependent_children and ...'. The person's own age in years. Differences: completed years at the survey reference date versus age when the card's eligibility is assessed (the module evaluates by year and states no date).

Consumed in nz/regulations/health_entitlement_cards/community_services_card/core.yaml by community_services_card_family_income_limit (source: Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 reg 8(5)) and community_services_card_superannuation_income_limit (reg 8(5A)): 'if community_services_card_person_married_or_partnered: <partnered limit> else: <single limits>'. Read as having a co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner. Differences: the regulations' test for married or partnered is not in this module; the concept is co-residence based, so a married person whose spouse lives elsewhere reads as unpartnered, and a cohabitation the regulations would not count is counted.

Consumed in nz/regulations/health_entitlement_cards/community_services_card/core.yaml by community_services_card_student_route (source: Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 reg 8(1)(f)): 'community_services_card_student_in_recognised_full_time_tertiary_course and community_services_card_ordinarily_resident_in_new_zealand and community_services_card_family_income_under_limit'. Read as enrolled full time in an ISCED 5-8 programme. Differences: the input requires a course that is recognised under the regulations (not defined in this module) and full time on that course's legal measure; the concept's full-time flag follows the programme's own definition and its tertiary band covers every ISCED 5-8 programme.

Consumed in nz/regulations/social_security/childcare_assistance/core.yaml by childcare_assistance_schedule_2_hourly_rate_before_fee_cap (source: Social Security Regulations 2018 Schedule 2): 'if childcare_assistance_dependent_children_count <= 1: ... else: if childcare_assistance_dependent_children_count == 2: ... else: <three-plus thresholds>' selects which set of income thresholds, compared with childcare_assistance_household_income_before_tax, fixes the hourly rate. The row is the caregiver (the module summary: s 77 gives assistance to a principal caregiver); read as the number of co-resident persons aged 17 or under who name this person as a parent (birth, adoptive or step). Differences: 'dependent child' is defined outside this module and the 17 cut is this mapping's assumption; children in the caregiver's care who do not name them as a parent (grandchildren, foster children, a partner's children not recorded as step) are missed.

nz/regulations/student_allowances/core.yaml rules student_allowance_has_recognised_partner (Student Allowances Regulations 1998 reg 2: '... or student_allowance_has_children'), student_allowance_weekly_gross_allowance (Schedule 2: 'if student_allowance_has_children: student_allowance_students_with_children_gross'); rate excerpts read 'the student has 1 or more supported children'. Difference: the regulations' 'supported child' definition is not encoded in the module; max_child_age 17 is this mapping's reading, and supported children with no parent pointer to the student are missed.

nz/regulations/student_allowances/core.yaml rule student_allowance_has_recognised_partner (Student Allowances Regulations 1998 reg 2): 'if student_allowance_has_partner and ((student_allowance_student_age >= student_allowance_partner_age_threshold and student_allowance_partner_age >= student_allowance_partner_age_threshold) or student_allowance_has_children): 1'. Difference: the regulations recognise a spouse or partner who lives apart (Schedule 2 has a rate for a student 'not living in the same home as their spouse or partner'); has_partner sees only a co-resident partner, and a survey cohabitant may not meet the regulations' partner definition.

nz/regulations/student_allowances/core.yaml rule student_allowance_lives_at_home (Student Allowances Regulations 1998 reg 2 and Schedule 2 clause 2): 'if student_allowance_has_recognised_partner > 0: if student_allowance_lives_with_partner: 1 else: 0'; rate excerpt 'is living in the same home as their spouse or partner'. The rule reads it only for a recognised partner, where a co-resident partner pointer is the same fact. Difference: the partner pointer is the survey's partner, which may not be the regulations' spouse or partner.

nz/regulations/student_allowances/core.yaml rules student_allowance_has_recognised_partner (reg 2: 'student_allowance_student_age >= student_allowance_partner_age_threshold', 24), student_allowance_single_student_no_children_gross and student_allowance_weekly_allowance (Schedule 2: 'student_allowance_student_age < student_allowance_rate_band_age_threshold', 24). Difference: the concept is age in completed years at the survey reference date; the rule reads the person's age when the entitlement is assessed, which the module does not date, so ages near the threshold can differ by the gap between the two dates.

Read by income_tax_activity_income_included (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 s MB 3; shared income-interface bridge for business and self-employment activity income'): 'max(0, income_tax_activity_income - income_tax_activity_deductions)'. The result is summed into income_tax_shared_income_bridge_total with the employment and schedular bridges. The input is gross activity income, with deductions in a separate input. The concepts are net non-farm and farm self-employment profit, so income_tax_activity_deductions stays uncovered (zero), and a net loss floors at zero instead of offsetting other income. Survey profit is not income as the Act measures it. Both sides are annual.

Read by income_tax_employment_income_included (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 s CE 1; shared income-interface bridge for employment, salary, and wage income'): 'max(0, income_tax_employment_income - income_tax_employment_deductions)'. The result is summed into income_tax_shared_income_bridge_total. The input is employment income as s CE 1 defines it. The concept is survey gross wages and salaries from all employee jobs, including overtime, tips, bonuses and commissions, and excluding benefits in kind and employer contributions. Anything s CE 1 counts beyond cash wages is missed. Both sides are annual.

Consumed in nz/statutes/income_tax/credits/individual_credits.yaml by charitable_or_public_benefit_gift_section_41a_refund_requirements (source: Tax Administration Act 1994 s 41A), whose formula includes 'and charitable_or_public_benefit_gift_refund_application_made'. A claiming decision, drawn like policyengine-us's would_file_if_eligible_for_refundable_credit (TakeUpThreshold us.refundable_credit_filing): true when the person's nz.donation_tax_credit draw from the persistent seed falls below a claim rate supplied at encode time. Differences: the value is imputed and independent of whether the person gave anything. The credit still needs the gift amounts and the other s 41A inputs (application in time, information provided, LD 1 requirements met), which stay uncovered, so this binding alone changes no credit.

Consumed in nz/statutes/income_tax/credits/individual_credits.yaml by independent_earner_tax_credit_status_requirement (source: Income Tax Act 2007 s LC 13(1)), whose formula includes 'and not independent_earner_tax_credit_receives_new_zealand_superannuation'; independent_earner_tax_credit is zero when that requirement fails. Read as positive(public_pension_income); the concept's definition names NZ Superannuation. Differences: other old-age pensions the concept holds also set the flag, such as an overseas state pension, or a Veteran's Pension recorded as a public pension (the rule tests Veteran's Pension through its own input). LC 13 tests receipt within a credit period, while the concept counts receipt at any time in the year, and this Year-period rule then zeroes the whole year's credit rather than only the months of receipt. Transport drops the concept, so the binding executes only on frames built from NZ's own data.

nz/statutes/income_tax/credits/individual_credits.yaml rule payroll_donation_credit_qualifies (Income Tax Act 2007 ss LD 4(1) and LD 8): 'payroll_donation_person_is_employee and payroll_donation_employer_files_employment_income_information_electronically and payroll_donation_employer_offers_payroll_giving and ...'. Difference: positive employee wages at any time in the reference year stands in for being an employee in the pay period the donation is made from.

Read by in_work_tax_credit_age_requirement (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 s MD 5'): 'in_work_tax_credit_person_age >= wff_minimum_age' (16, ss MC 3 and MD 5). The input is the claimant's age, held on the Family entity. The binding takes the Family reference member's age in completed years at the survey reference date. The claimant need not be the reference member, and the dates differ.

nz/statutes/income_tax/family_scheme/eligibility.yaml rule wff_principal_care_requirement (Income Tax Act 2007 s MC 4): 'wff_dependent_children_principal_caregiver_count >= 1' (test values 1 and 2); the module reads the count nowhere else. Group rule reference_member: counts co-resident persons aged 17 or under who name the Family's principal member as a parent (birth, adoptive or step). Difference: principal caregiver is a Commissioner determination (s MC 10; the separate input wff_commissioner_considers_primary_day_to_day_care). Children with no parent pointer to the principal member are missed, so a Family whose principal member is not recorded as the children's parent (for example a step-parent without a step-parent pointer while the partner is the recorded parent) counts zero and fails s MC 4. max_age 17 is this mapping's reading of 'dependent child', and the module handles an 18-year-old in school separately (s MC 9(1), wff_credit_child_school_tertiary_age = 18), which this count leaves out.

nz/statutes/income_tax/family_scheme/eligibility.yaml rule wff_person_age_requirement (Income Tax Act 2007 s MC 3): 'wff_person_age >= wff_minimum_age', parameter 16. Group rule reference_member: the Family's principal member stands in for 'the person' claiming, whom the concepts do not identify. Difference: the concept is age in completed years at the survey reference date; the rule reads the person's age when the entitlement is assessed, which the module does not date, so ages near the threshold can differ by the gap between the two dates.

Read by family_scheme_activity_income_included (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 s MB 3(2)'): 'max(0, family_scheme_activity_income - family_scheme_activity_deductions)'. family_scheme_income_before_period_adjustment (ss MB 1 and MB 3 to MB 13) adds the result to family_scheme_base_income_excluding_mb3_to_mb13_adjustments. The input is gross income from an activity, with its deductions in a separate input. The concepts are net non-farm and farm self-employment profit, so family_scheme_activity_deductions stays uncovered (zero) and the rule's floor at zero drops a net loss. Members' profits are summed onto the Family entity. Because signed profits are summed across members and across farm and non-farm activity before the rule's single zero floor, one member's or one activity's loss offsets another's profit, which the Family-level input cannot separate. The module does not say whether its Family-level amount is one person's or a couple's family scheme income. A dependent child's profit would also be summed here, although the module handles dependent-child income separately (MB 11). Survey profit is not activity income as the Act measures it.

Read by in_work_tax_credit_relevant_children (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 s MD 10(3)(c)'): 'max(wff_in_work_tax_credit_minimum_children_for_base_amount, max(0, in_work_tax_credit_allowed_children_count))', where the minimum is 3. This scales in_work_tax_credit_before_abatement (s MD 10(2)) only when the uncovered input entitled_to_in_work_tax_credit is true. The module's test pairs a count of 2 with one eldest and one subsequent family-tax-credit child. The binding takes the Family reference member's count of co-resident persons aged 17 or under who name them as a parent. Differences: eligibility.yaml tests children through principal-caregiver and financial-dependency predicates (in_work_tax_credit_principal_caregiver, in_work_tax_credit_child_financially_dependent) that the concepts cannot evaluate. It also carries an MC 9(1) age parameter of 18 (wff_credit_child_school_tertiary_age) that the age-17 cut-off ignores. A reference member who is not the children's named parent counts zero.

Read by fb_entitled (source 'Income Tax Act 2007 ss MH 3(1), MH 3(6)-(7)'): 'not (has_relationship_partner and not separated_with_no_partner_at_quarter_end and relationship_partner_is_couples_claimant_for_quarter)'. Also read by fb_tax_credit_income (s MH 4(7)-(8)): 'if has_relationship_partner and not separated_with_no_partner_at_quarter_end: partner_tax_credit_income_for_quarter'. The input is the Act's relationship-partner status for a tax credit quarter. The concept flags a co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner at one survey reference date. It misses a partner the Act would count who lives elsewhere, and it cannot see changes within the quarter.

nz/statutes/income_tax/withholding/resident_withholding_tax.yaml rule rwt_withholding_amount (Income Tax Act 2007 subpart RE, cited at s RE 12): 'max(0, rwt_gross_interest_and_dividends) * rwt_applicable_rate', rule period Year; module summary 'resident withholding tax rates applied to interest and dividends for New Zealand residents'. Difference: the input is the interest and dividends RWT is withheld from, which the module does not define further; the survey totals (gross of tax withheld) can include amounts outside NZ withholding, such as foreign-paid interest or dividends, and any dividend-specific withholding adjustments are not encoded here.

Read by kiwisaver_employee_deduction (source 'KiwiSaver Act 2006 s 64; Inland Revenue KiwiSaver contribution guidance'): 'max(0, kiwisaver_gross_salary_or_wages) * kiwisaver_selected_employee_contribution_rate'. Also read by kiwisaver_minimum_employer_contribution ('KiwiSaver Act 2006 s 101B'): 'max(0, kiwisaver_gross_salary_or_wages) * kiwisaver_employer_minimum_contribution_rate'. The input is the gross salary or wages that KiwiSaver contributions are taken from. The concept is survey gross wages and salaries from all employee jobs, including tips and bonuses and excluding benefits in kind. Neither rule reads KiwiSaver membership, so the employer contribution is computed on every employee's wages. The employee rate is an election and stays uncovered. Both sides are annual.

nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/core.yaml rule nz_super_age_requirement (NZ Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 s 7): 'nz_super_person_age >= nz_super_age_threshold and not nz_super_elected_weekly_compensation_instead_of_superannuation', threshold parameter 65. Difference: the concept is age in completed years at the survey reference date; the rule reads the person's age when the entitlement is assessed, which the module does not date, so ages near the threshold can differ by the gap between the two dates.

nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/core.yaml rules nz_super_living_alone (s 4A: 'nz_super_single and nz_super_principal_residence_is_qualifying_accommodation and ...') and nz_super_ordinary_weekly_rate_before_tax (s 12 and Schedule 1 Part 1 clause 1: 'if nz_super_single: ... else: nz_super_partnered_weekly_rate_before_tax'); nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/special_rates.yaml rule nz_super_hospital_rate_population (s 19(2): 'nz_super_single or (nz_super_in_relationship and not nz_super_has_dependent_children)'). Difference: no_partner means no co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner. The module does not define 'single'; a person whose spouse or partner lives elsewhere (for example in care) has no partner pointer and reads single here, and a survey-recorded cohabitant may not meet the Act's relationship test.

nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/special_rates.yaml rule nz_super_hospital_rate_population (NZ Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 s 19(2)): '... or (nz_super_in_relationship and not nz_super_has_dependent_children)'. Difference: flags a person named as parent (birth, adoptive or step) by a co-resident person aged 17 or under. max_child_age 17 is this mapping's reading of 'dependent child' as under 18; the module does not encode the definition's age limit or its care and financial-dependence tests, and dependent children with no parent pointer to the person (or living elsewhere) are missed.

nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/special_rates.yaml rule nz_super_hospital_rate_population (NZ Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 s 19(2)): 'nz_super_receives_or_becomes_entitled and (nz_super_single or (nz_super_in_relationship and not nz_super_has_dependent_children))'. Difference: has_partner means a co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner; a partner living elsewhere is missed, and a survey-recorded cohabitant may not meet the Act's relationship test.

Consumed in nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/special_rates.yaml by nz_super_hospital_rate_population (source: New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 s 19(2)), which ANDs 'nz_super_receives_or_becomes_entitled' with single status or partnered status without dependent children. Read as positive(public_pension_income); the concept's definition names NZ Superannuation. Differences: the input also covers a person who becomes entitled, which reference-year receipt does not show; other old-age pensions the concept holds also set the flag, such as an overseas state pension or a Veteran's Pension recorded as a public pension; and the concept is an annual amount. The module's hospital inputs stay uncovered, so the flag matters only once they are fed. Transport drops the concept, so the binding executes only on frames built from NZ's own data.

nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/core.yaml rules nz_super_living_alone (s 4A: 'nz_super_single and nz_super_principal_residence_is_qualifying_accommodation and ...') and nz_super_ordinary_weekly_rate_before_tax (s 12 and Schedule 1 Part 1 clause 1: 'if nz_super_single: ... else: nz_super_partnered_weekly_rate_before_tax'); nz/statutes/new_zealand_superannuation/special_rates.yaml rule nz_super_hospital_rate_population (s 19(2): 'nz_super_single or (nz_super_in_relationship and not nz_super_has_dependent_children)'). Difference: no_partner means no co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner. The module does not define 'single'; a person whose spouse or partner lives elsewhere (for example in care) has no partner pointer and reads single here, and a survey-recorded cohabitant may not meet the Act's relationship test.

nz/statutes/parental_leave/paid_parental_leave.yaml rule ppl_entitlement_for_employee (Parental Leave and Employment Protection Act 1987 s 71B): 'if ppl_employee_is_eligible: min(max(0, ppl_employees_average_weekly_earnings), ppl_maximum_weekly_rate)', rule period Week; module summary 'The weekly PPL rate is the lower of the employee's average weekly earnings and the maximum PPL rate'. Scale 1/52: weekly = annual / 52. Difference: reference-year employee wages averaged over 52 weeks, against the Act's average weekly earnings over a pre-leave window the module does not state; self-employment earnings are not included.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_cash_assets_within_limit (source: Social Security Act 2018 s 65(1)(b); Social Security Regulations 2018 reg 15). It holds when accommodation_supplement_cash_assets is at most accommodation_supplement_cash_asset_limit_partnered_or_with_children (16200, reg 15(1)(a)) for a family in a relationship or with dependent children, and at most accommodation_supplement_cash_asset_limit_other (8100, reg 15(1)(b)) otherwise, and accommodation_supplement_non_rate_entitlement_requirements (ss 65 to 67) requires it. The module does not define cash assets. The Act does, in s 68(2), which Schedule 2 applies for the purposes of the accommodation supplement: money saved, invested or banked with a bank or other institution; money invested in securities, bonds or debentures, or advanced on mortgage; money withdrawn from a KiwiSaver scheme; and money invested in shares in a partnership, company or other body. It excludes KiwiSaver contributions and member's interests, and anything the regulations exempt (reg 16 and Schedule 8 Part 1). Under s 69(2), which reg 15(3) restates, an applicant's assets include those of their spouse or partner, so the binding sums members' amounts onto the Family entity. It is deferred: no code applies it until a future unit-construction step builds Family units, and that step's unit rule will decide who is a member. Differences: the concept leaves out money advanced on mortgage, withdrawn KiwiSaver money held as cash, shares in a partnership or company the person runs, which s 68(2)(a)(iv) counts as money invested in shares in a partnership or limited liability company or other incorporated or unincorporated body (a sole trader's non-cash business equity is in neither), and a member's interest in a non-KiwiSaver superannuation scheme, which Schedule 8 item 10 exempts only while a lock-in clause prevents withdrawal (Schedule 8 cl 25); the other Schedule 8 exemptions are not applied; if the unit rule makes a dependent child a Family member, the child's assets will be summed too, although s 69(2) adds only a spouse's or partner's, and if it leaves out a spouse or partner in long-term residential care, whose assets s 69(2A) still counts, their assets will be missed; and the concept is the stock at the survey reference date, while the test applies when the supplement is assessed.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_entry_threshold_rate (source: Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 7 clauses 1 to 6): 'if accommodation_supplement_costs_are_homeownership: accommodation_supplement_homeownership_entry_threshold_rate else: accommodation_supplement_rent_board_entry_threshold_rate'. Read as the household owning its dwelling (outright or with a mortgage). Differences: the input describes this family's own accommodation costs; household_value gives every family in an owner-occupied household true, including a second family (a boarder or other resident) whose costs are board or rent, not homeownership costs.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_non_rate_entitlement_requirements (source: Social Security Act 2018 ss 65 to 67): 'accommodation_supplement_has_accommodation_costs and accommodation_supplement_cash_assets_within_limit and ...'. The module computes the amount of weekly accommodation costs separately, in accommodation_supplement_weekly_accommodation_costs (source: s 65AAA definition of accommodation costs), from other inputs; nothing in the module ties this gate to that amount or says what counts as having accommodation costs. Read as any tenure other than rent_free. Differences: the input asks whether this family itself has accommodation costs; household_value gives true to every family in a rented or owned household, including a family that pays nothing toward housing, and the legal components of accommodation costs are not checked.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_cash_assets_within_limit (reg 15 asset limits) and accommodation_supplement_maximum_weekly_rate (Schedule 4 Part 7 clauses 1 to 6: 'accommodation_supplement_in_relationship and accommodation_supplement_has_dependent_children' selects the large-family rates). Read as any family member being the parent (birth, adoptive or step) of a co-resident person aged 17 or under. Differences: 'dependent child' is a Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 2 term that this module does not define; the age cut at 17 is this mapping's assumption, not read from the Act; a non-parent caregiver's child is missed and a co-resident child who would not count as dependent is included.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_cash_assets_within_limit (source: Social Security Act 2018 s 65(1)(b); Social Security Regulations 2018 reg 15), which picks the partnered-or-with-children cash asset limit, and by accommodation_supplement_maximum_weekly_rate (Schedule 4 Part 7 clauses 1 to 6), which picks the family category. Read as the family's reference member having a co-resident spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner. Differences: the Act's test for being in a relationship is not in this module; the concept is co-residence based, so a partner living elsewhere is missed and a cohabitation the Act would not treat as a relationship is counted.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_social_housing_exclusion_not_applies (source: Social Security Act 2018 s 66): 'not accommodation_supplement_rent_paid_to_kainga_ora and not accommodation_supplement_rent_paid_to_registered_community_housing_provider_social_housing and not accommodation_supplement_concessionary_mortgage_payments_to_kainga_ora_or_crown'. The tenure concept's rented_public_authority category names NZ Kainga Ora as its public landlord. The input is narrower: it is one landlord, not any public authority, and it is this family's rent, while household_value gives true to every family in the household, including one that does not itself pay rent to Kainga Ora.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_social_housing_exclusion_not_applies (source: Social Security Act 2018 s 66), alongside the Kainga Ora and concessionary-mortgage exclusions. The tenure concept's rented_nonprofit_social category names the NZ registered community housing provider as its non-profit social landlord. The input is narrower: a registered provider and a social-housing tenancy, and this family's own rent, while household_value gives true to every family in the household.

Consumed in nz/statutes/social_security/accommodation_supplement/core.yaml by accommodation_supplement_weekly_accommodation_costs (source: Social Security Act 2018 s 65AAA definition of accommodation costs), whose last branch returns accommodation_supplement_weekly_rent_paid when the family is not an owner, a joint owner with a resident, an additional resident in social housing or a boarder; the result feeds the Schedule 4 Part 7 weekly formula against weekly maximum rates (the module's tests feed weekly rents such as 700). Scale 1/52 turns the concept's annual contract rent into an average weekly amount; the rule declares period Year but the value is weekly. Differences: the concept is contract rent for the whole dwelling before housing subsidy, excluding separately billed utilities and service charges, and s 65AAA's own definition of rent is not in this module; the household amount goes to the family containing the household reference person, so another family in the household that pays the tenant gets zero here (in the rule's terms it pays board or contributions, which stay uncovered).

Read by disability_allowance_income_limit (source 'Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 5 Part 3'). 'disability_allowance_dependent_children_count <= 1' picks the sole-parent one-child limit (clause 13) over clause 14, and '== 0' is one condition of the 16-or-17 single limit (clause 10).
